input.quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
input.rationale: Article III is a one-way ownership clause: Licensor owns the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and "Derivative Work" (1.3) sweeps in "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements based upon or incorporating the Licensed Technology". Licensor keeping its platform IP is expected and not objectionable, but there is no counterpart anywhere in the Agreement confirming that we retain rights in our own data (trade records, orders, reports we are required to generate and submit under Article V.IV and Article VII(e)) or in our pre-existing IP, and the definition of "Intellectual Property Rights" is drafted as rights "of Licensor" only. In addition, the custom development we pay for under Article VII(b) (a "unique client front end and other enhancements") falls within Derivative Work and so is captured by Licensor's ownership, leaving us with only the non-exclusive, Field-of-Use-limited licence for the term (Article IV renewal being at Licensor's option) — no ownership and no perpetual, irrevocable licence back. That fails both the preferred and the fallback position on the material terms (customer ownership of what it pays for / perpetual licence-back, and retention of Customer Data). The redline adds a minimal carve-out to Article III: we retain our data and pre-existing IP with no assignment and no joint ownership, and customizations we fund are assigned to us with Licensor retaining its pre-existing platform IP and granting a perpetual, royalty-free licence to any embedded Licensor IP.

proposal.summary: Add Licensee Data / customization ownership carve-out to Article III Ownership
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article III gives Licensor ownership of the Licensed Technology and all Derivative Works with no carve-out, so our trading and client data and the customization work we pay for under Article VII(b) would sit with Licensor. We have added a short carve-out confirming we retain our data and pre-existing IP (no assignment, no joint ownership) and that customizations we fund are ours, with Licensor keeping its platform IP and granting us a perpetual licence to any of its IP embedded in them. If ownership of the customizations is an issue, we can instead take a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense them.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing: (i) Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, orders, trade records, reports, configurations and other content submitted by or generated for Licensee through the Licensed Technology ("Licensee Data"), and in and to Licensee's pre-existing intellectual property, and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Licensor, or creates any joint ownership in, any Licensee Data or any Licensee intellectual property; and (ii) Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest in and to any customization, unique client front end or other work product developed for Licensee and paid for by Licensee pursuant to Article VII(b), provided that Licensor retains ownership of its pre-existing Licensed Technology and hereby grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify and sublicense any Licensor intellectual property embedded in such work product for Licensee's business purposes.
